prompt_package.goal_summary: Turn one phone photo of a product into a clean, on-brand catalog hero shot in one run.

user_profile.who: Small shop owner with no design training

blocks.task: Create a clean e-commerce hero photo of {{product_name}} using the attached photo as the exact source for its shape, label and color.
blocks.subject: {{product_name}}, unchanged in shape, label text and material. {{key_detail}}.
blocks.scene: The product stands on {{surface}}. Behind it is a smooth {{brand_color}} backdrop that darkens slightly at the edges. Nothing else is in the frame.
blocks.camera: Eye level with a slight top-down tilt, 100mm macro look, product fills about 70% of the frame with even space on all four sides.
blocks.light: Large softbox from the top left, white bounce card on the right, soft contact shadow under the product, thin rim highlight on the left edge.
locks: Label text, spelling, logo shape and color stay exactly as in the reference photo.
Product proportions stay the same. No reshaping and no extra parts.
avoid: extra props or hands in frame
words, badges or watermarks I did not ask for

input_schema.description: Fill these values before you run. Every {{name}} in the prompt comes from here.

fields.name: key_detail
fields.example: A cotton wick, unlit, with a small paper seal on the lid
fields.default: A clean, unmarked top with no fingerprints

fields.name: material
fields.example: frosted amber glass with a matte black lid

fields.name: reference_photo
fields.example: IMG_2041.jpg, shot on a kitchen table

output_schema.description: What you get back, plus how to accept or reject it.

fields.name: accept_if
example: label is readable at phone size

example_input.material: frosted amber glass with a matte black lid
example_input.key_detail: A cotton wick, unlit, with a small paper seal on the lid

accept_if: glass has a soft window reflection
floor shadow is soft and short

examples.title: Soap bar on linen, sage background

example_input.material: matte cold-press soap with stamped lettering
example_input.key_detail: One bar, slightly angled, paper band halfway up

non_obvious_insights: The reference photo is the real product. Say 'exact source for shape, label and color' in the first line, or the model will redesign your packaging.
Ask for 70% frame fill. Products at 90% look cramped on mobile feeds, and products at 40% look like stock photos.
A soft contact shadow is the cheapest realism upgrade. Without it the product floats.
Never let the model redraw fine print. Crop the reference so the label is large when you upload it; small label input equals invented letters.
Generate at 1K for the first pass, then re-run the winner at 2K. 1K and 2K cost the same on this model, so 2K is the default for delivery.
4:5 beats 1:1 for marketplaces and Instagram grid. One canvas serves both.
monetization_ideas: Offer a '10 products in one day' catalog pack to local shops. Same package, different variables.
Sell the filled JSON as a product-photo kit with a one-page checklist; the buyer fills the blanks themselves.
Bundle a monthly retainer: 20 refreshed hero shots per month for one store, priced under a studio day.
License the template to print-on-demand sellers who need consistent mockups across many SKUs.
prompt_package.reusability_notes: Swap surface, backdrop and light for cosmetics, drinks, jewelry or ceramics. Change aspect_ratio to 1:1 for marketplaces, 16:9 for banners, 9:16 for stories. The same variables drive every channel, so one shoot becomes five placements. For a lifestyle version, add a hand and change scene only; keep locks untouched.
